primary_sources: GitHub Actions & GitLab Enterprise CI/CD Guidelines

rules.explanation: Merging pull requests or building release artifacts without triggering automated test suites risks shipping critical regressions to production environments.
rules.do: Enforce mandatory automated unit, integration, and security scanning jobs on all pull request events before allowing branch merges.
rules.dont: Do not bypass automated CI pipeline test checks or approve production deployments with failing test steps.

rules.explanation: Hardcoding API keys or cloud credentials directly in source control or CI logs creates massive security compromises.
rules.do: Inject environment variables dynamically using dedicated secret management vaults (e.g., HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, GitHub Encrypted Secrets).
rules.dont: Do not commit plain-text credentials to configuration files or print sensitive token variables into pipeline stdout logs.

rules.explanation: Directly replacing running production application instances without traffic redirection causes downtime and dropped client connections during updates.
rules.do: Implement zero-downtime deployment patterns such as Blue-Green, Rolling Updates, or Canary releases with health-check verification.
rules.dont: Do not perform in-place restarts on single active production server nodes during peak business hours.

rules.rule_name: Pipeline Artifact Caching and Build Efficiency
rules.explanation: Downloading large language dependencies and package archives on every CI execution wastes bandwidth and delays developer feedback loops.
rules.do: Configure intelligent layer and dependency caching (e.g., npm, pip, Docker layer caches) to optimize job execution times.
rules.dont: Do not run un-cached fresh package installations from scratch on every minor commit step.
